## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** With VS Code as the default editor and uwsm's default scope launch, `omarchy-launch-editor --inline` now blocks until VS Code closes the file, which addresses #13037. One mapped flag is not accepted by its editor, and the new blocking also reaches Omarchy's own directory-opening `$EDITOR` callers.

Launch chain for `git commit` with VS Code (traced through uwsm 0.26.7, util-linux `setsid`, systemd-run and VS Code 1.125.0 source):

```text
git: sh -c "$EDITOR <file>"
 └─ omarchy-launch-editor --inline
     └─ setsid -w      forks only if the launcher leads its process group; -w then waits and returns the editor's status
         └─ uwsm-app   execs systemd-run --user --scope (synchronous)
             └─ code --wait -- <file>   returns when the file is closed
```

**Verified** in an isolated sandbox with the real `setsid` and stub editors (a stub that sleeps and exits 7):

| Check | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| Launcher as process-group leader, inline | returns 0 at once while the editor still runs | waits, returns 7 |
| Launcher as plain child (as under git), inline | execs through, returns 7 | execs through, returns 7 |
| Non-inline and TUI argv, 17 editor names | identical | identical |
| PR test `test/shell.d/launch-editor-test.sh` | fails at "inline launch passes --wait to code" | passes |

The wait flags match editor source or documentation for VS Code (also code-insiders and codium), Zed (`--wait`), Sublime Text (`-w`) and gedit (`--wait`).

### `gnome-text-editor` does not accept `--wait`

GNOME Text Editor 44.0 through 51.0 and current `main` register only `--ignore-session`, `--new-window`, `--standalone` and `--version` (`src/editor-application.c`). Because the app registers its own options, GLib treats the unknown `--wait` as a parse error and exits 1 before opening anything. This is established from source; the real binary was not run.

```text
default editor = gnome-text-editor, --inline
base: gnome-text-editor -- <file>          file opens (launcher does not wait)
head: gnome-text-editor --wait -- <file>   option parse error, exit 1, file never opens
```

**Impact:** Inline launches with this editor stop opening the file, and `git commit` aborts with "there was a problem with the editor". Reach is limited: `omarchy-default-editor` does not offer this editor, so only a manually written defaults file is affected.

**Suggested change:** Remove `gnome-text-editor` from the `--wait` group so it takes the unknown-GUI path. Keep `gedit --wait`, which gedit supports.

### Omarchy's directory-opening `$EDITOR` callers now wait for the editor window

`$EDITOR` defaults to `omarchy-launch-editor --inline` (`default/bash/envs`). Some Omarchy flows use it to open a project directory and continue. VS Code's `--wait` on a folder returns only when that window closes or loads another folder, and Zed documents the same for directories.

| Caller | Base (GUI editor) | Head (GUI editor) |
|---|---|---|
| Plugin menu "Clone" (`omarchy-plugin-clone --edit`) | editor opens, floating terminal reaches its Done prompt | floating terminal stays open until the project window closes |
| `tdl` / `hdl` editor pane (`$EDITOR .`) | pane returns to its prompt | pane stays occupied until the project window closes |
| `eff` alias on a file | returns after hand-off | waits until the file tab closes (the intended `--inline` behavior) |

These outcomes follow from source and process-group experiments with stub editors, not from runs of real GUI editors.

**Impact:** Workflow change only. The clone and the layout complete as before. The blocking matches the `--inline` contract, but the directory-opening callers appear to expect launch-and-continue.

**Suggested change:** If launch-and-continue is intended there, give plugin clone `--edit` and the `tdl` / `hdl` editor pane a non-waiting launch for GUI editors. The plain non-inline launcher would also move TUI editors into a new terminal, so a GUI-only choice may fit better. Otherwise, mention the change in the PR description, which currently says only that non-inline launches stay detached.

**Optional:** uwsm supports `UWSM_APP_UNIT_TYPE=service` in its app daemon environment. Omarchy does not set it, but with it `uwsm-app` starts a transient service without waiting, so inline launches would return early again. Passing `-t scope` to `uwsm-app` in the inline branch makes the wait independent of that setting.

**Documentation note:** The PR description says the test covers TUI, known GUI and unknown GUI editors in both inline and non-inline modes. Only `code` has a non-inline case.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the launcher, the added test and Omarchy's `$EDITOR` callers, plus upstream source of uwsm 0.26.7, util-linux `setsid`, systemd-run, git, VS Code 1.125.0, Zed, gedit and GNOME Text Editor. The PR test, an argv matrix and process-group experiments ran in an isolated sandbox with stub editors. No GUI editor, uwsm daemon or desktop session was run, so editor wait behavior comes from source and documentation. Cursor, Windsurf and Sublime Text directory handling were not verified.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
